title: Advanced passive / reporting
note: impersonal It is said / was announced / has been suggested + that-clause · raised subject with the to-infinitive carrying the time (to be / to have been / to be doing / to have been doing) · the passive across every tense, aspect, modal and non-finite form · get-passive register and the by-agent, including passives of ditransitives · 4 strands x 12 · 48 items · built to live 2026-08-07 (cloud run 13)

cards.title: Reporting without naming the source
cards.title_cz: Jak sdělit tvrzení, aniž řeknete kdo
cards.body: The passive earns its keep when the agent is unknown, obvious, or deliberately kept out of the frame. At C1 that shows up most in reporting: a newspaper, a report or a paper needs to say what is claimed without standing behind the claim itself. English has two ready-made frames for exactly this, and Czech covers both with a reflexive.
cards.body_cz: Trpný rod se vyplatí tam, kde původce není znám, je zřejmý, nebo ho záměrně necháváme stranou. Na úrovni C1 se to nejčastěji projeví u uvození řeči: noviny, zpráva nebo odborný text potřebují sdělit, co se tvrdí, aniž by se za to tvrzení postavily. Angličtina má na to dvě hotové vazby, čeština obě pokrývá zvratnou formou.

table.caption: one claim, three ways to say it
rows: People say that she has left.
It is said that she has left.
She is said to have left.

cards.title: It is said that…
cards.title_cz: It is said that… — neosobní vazba
cards.body: Dummy It holds the subject position, the reporting verb goes passive, and the content follows in a full that-clause. Tense lives on the passive group, not on the that-clause, so the reporting can be present, past or recent while the content stays whatever it was.
cards.body_cz: Formální It drží podmětnou pozici, sloveso uvození jde do trpného rodu a obsah následuje v celé vedlejší větě s that. Čas nese trpný tvar, nikoli vedlejší věta — uvození tak může být přítomné, minulé i nedávné, zatímco obsah zůstane, jaký byl.

table.caption: tense sits on the passive group

points: The that-clause is a full clause — it keeps its own subject and finite verb
Adverbs go inside the group: It is widely expected that…
Works with say, believe, think, report, claim, expect, understand, fear, accept

cards.title: Raising the subject
cards.body: The second frame promotes the person into the main clause and turns the rest into a to-infinitive. Which infinitive you pick is the whole skill: it encodes when the reported event happened relative to the reporting.
cards.body_cz: Druhá vazba vytáhne osobu do věty hlavní a zbytek promění v infinitiv s to. Právě volba infinitivu je tu celá dovednost: kóduje, kdy se uváděný děj odehrál vzhledem k okamžiku uvození.

table.caption: the infinitive carries the time
rows: He is believed to be ill.
He is said to be living abroad.
She is thought to have left.
The bridge is said to have been built in 1850.
They are said to have been working on it for years.

points: It is said that she left. = She is said to have left.
Negation goes on the reporting verb: She is not thought to be involved.

cards.title: The passive in every tense
cards.body: None of this is a separate grammar. The main verb sits in the past participle and never moves; be takes whatever shape the tense, aspect or modal demands. Learn the shape of be and the rest follows.
cards.body_cz: Nejde o žádnou zvláštní gramatiku. Významové sloveso stojí v příčestí trpném a nehýbe se; sloveso be dostane tvar, který si žádá čas, vid nebo způsobové sloveso. Naučte se tvary be a zbytek plyne sám.

table.caption: same verb, ten shapes of be
rows: The machine will have been repaired.
The office is going to be painted.
The email should have been sent.

cards.title: get instead of be
cards.body: The get-passive is informal and carries a nudge of meaning that be does not: something happened to the subject, often suddenly and often to their cost or benefit. It sits well in speech and badly in a formal report.
cards.body_cz: Trpný rod s get je hovorový a nese významový odstín, který be nemá: podmět něco potkalo, často náhle a často k jeho škodě nebo prospěchu. V mluveném projevu sedí dobře, ve formální zprávě špatně.
points: get + past participle — no be anywhere in the group
Avoid it in academic writing and formal reports
It leans towards events, not states: got broken ✓ · gets known ✗

cards.title: Common mistakes

table.caption: check
rows: It is said that she left.
It is said she to leave.
She is said to have left.
She is said that she left.
The email should have been sent.

points: been is the participle, being is the -ing form — they are not interchangeable
Add by + agent only when the agent is news

items.en: It is said that the company is in trouble.
items.cz: Říká se, že firma je v potížích.
items.gap: ____ that the company is in trouble.
accepts: It is said that the company is in trouble.
items.explanation: The impersonal passive lets English report a claim without naming who makes it: a dummy It fills the subject slot, the reporting verb goes into the passive, and the whole proposition follows in a that-clause. Tense sits on the passive verb group — It is said (now), It was announced (then), It has been suggested (recent). This is the standard register of news, academic writing and formal reports, where Czech normally reaches for a reflexive instead.
items.explanation_cz: Neosobní trpný rod umožňuje angličtině sdělit tvrzení, aniž pojmenuje jeho původce: podmětnou pozici zaujme formální It, sloveso uvození se dá do trpného rodu a celý obsah následuje ve vedlejší větě s that. Čas nese trpný tvar slovesa — It is said (teď), It was announced (tehdy), It has been suggested (nedávno). Je to běžný rejstřík zpravodajství, odborných textů a formálních zpráv; čeština tu obvykle volí zvratnou formu.

items.explanation: The same report can be built around the person instead of a dummy It: the subject of the that-clause is raised into the main clause and the rest becomes a to-infinitive. The infinitive carries the time — to be for now, to have been for earlier, to be doing for something in progress, to have been doing for a stretch running up to now. Only reporting verbs allow this, and the result stays formal.
items.explanation_cz: Totéž sdělení lze postavit kolem osoby místo formálního It: podmět vedlejší věty se vytáhne do věty hlavní a zbytek se změní na infinitiv s to. Čas nese právě infinitiv — to be pro přítomnost, to have been pro dřívější děj, to be doing pro děj probíhající a to have been doing pro děj trvající až doteď. Tuhle vazbu dovolují jen slovesa uvození a věta zůstává formální.

items.explanation: Two further choices decide how a passive lands. First, get instead of be: informal, and it pushes the event towards something that happened to the subject, often suddenly or unluckily. Second, the agent: by + agent is added only when it carries information — most passives leave it out precisely because who did it is unknown or beside the point. Verbs with two objects can raise either one, and English strongly prefers the person.
items.explanation_cz: O tom, jak trpná věta vyzní, rozhodují dvě další volby. Za prvé get místo be: je hovorové a posouvá děj k něčemu, co podmět potkalo, často náhle nebo nemile. Za druhé původce: by + původce se doplní jen tehdy, když nese informaci — většina trpných vět ho vynechává právě proto, že původce není znám nebo na něm nezáleží. Slovesa se dvěma předměty mohou do podmětu vytáhnout kterýkoli z nich a angličtina jasně upřednostňuje osobu.
